title: A decision can be deprecated; the views show only what stands
situation: A fresh session reading the decisions or the state met about a hundred and thirty settled decisions, most of them about finished pieces of work or now stated by the concepts, and had to sort them by hand.
decision: A decision stands until it is superseded or deprecated. Deprecated is the established status of an architecture decision that no longer applies and has no replacement: a later entry names it and says why, and it is kept as history. A decision may name the cut it was about; once that cut is integrated, the decision is deprecated without any entry. The journal's views show only standing decisions, and show history only when asked. The same holds for examples: a cut's examples are history once the cut is integrated, unless a standing decision keeps them.
consequences: The record's settled decisions about finished work are deprecated now; the views read small enough for a fresh session.
